prior_result.explanation: Claude did flip to familiar=true with an accurate, detailed answer sourced from search, but the current title is still "The martech problem index" with no domain string, so the 2026-09 change appears never to have been applied (or was reverted) and the flip cannot be attributed to it.

proposal.observation: All three models are now familiar, all on basis=search_results, and all three correctly describe the monthly ranked board, the three-model panel, and the open data. Coverage of the self-measurement piece is uneven: ChatGPT names the public recognition log, Claude and Gemini do not, and Gemini also omits the shared answer formats.
proposal.hypothesis: The models' summaries are driven largely by the meta description: if the recognition log is named there, Claude and Gemini should start mentioning it in the 2026-11 log; if neither does while ChatGPT still does, the meta description is not the source and the answers are being built from page body and navigation instead.

change.current_text: Each month, ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini name the hardest unsolved problems in marketing technology. Each day, all three explain how they would attack one of them, in the same format, side by side. Open data, open harness.
change.proposed_text: Each month, ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini name the hardest unsolved problems in marketing technology. Each day, all three explain how they would attack one of them, in the same format, side by side. A public recognition log records what those same models say this site is. Open data, open harness.
change.rationale: One appended sentence, nothing removed, so any change in how the models describe the site is attributable to it. The recognition log is the one true, distinctive feature that two of three models currently omit, which makes it a clean marker for tracing which surface they are reading.

proposal.expected_signal: In the 2026-11 log, Claude and/or Gemini name the public recognition log (or the site asking models what it is) without losing the board, daily answers, or open data elements already present.
